input.body:
label: bug
file: src/export/scheduler.ts

`nextRunAt` in this file only guards against scheduling in the past for the `daily` cadence (`if (next <= from) next.setUTCDate(...)`). For `weekly` and `monthly` it unconditionally jumps forward by 7 days / to next month, even when the computed run time (today at RUN_HOUR_UTC) is still in the future relative to `from`.

This explains the report: a weekly schedule created at 05:40 UTC (before the 06:00 UTC run hour) should fire that same morning, but instead always gets pushed a full week ahead, so the first export is silently skipped. priya-s's test schedule, created at 09:00 UTC (after the run hour), happened to need the extra week anyway, so it looked correct.

Fix: apply the same "only advance if the computed next run is not after `from`" check to the weekly and monthly branches (or more precisely, only add the period when the computed same-day/month run time is `<= from`).

input.title: Fix weekly export schedules skipping their first run
input.body:
File: src/export/scheduler.ts

In `nextRunAt`, the `daily` case correctly checks `if (next <= from) next.setUTCDate(next.getUTCDate() + 1);` before advancing, so a schedule created earlier in the day than `RUN_HOUR_UTC` still fires that same day. The `weekly` case has no such check: it unconditionally does `next.setUTCDate(next.getUTCDate() + 7);` regardless of whether the computed run time (today at `RUN_HOUR_UTC`) is still ahead of `from`.

This is why a weekly schedule created early in the morning (e.g. 05:40 UTC, before the 06:00 UTC run hour) skips its first intended run: instead of firing later that same day, it jumps a full week ahead, so no export goes out until the following week — matching the reporter's observation that the first weekly export never arrives.

Proposed fix: mirror the daily logic for the weekly branch — only advance by 7 days when the computed time (`next`) is not still strictly after `from`; otherwise leave it at today's `RUN_HOUR_UTC` so the first run happens on schedule.
